newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels ends talks with Rank.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels ends talks with Rank.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. and Britain's Rank Group Plc said Monday they have ended talks on Rank purchasing a $50 million equity stake in and changing the theme of Trump's Castle in Atlantic City, N.J.

For three months Trump Hotels had been trying to sell up to 50 percent of Trump's Castle to Rank, a British leisure and entertainment company, to turn into a Hard Rock Casino Hotel. Rank had been expected to share in the resort's profits.

"We explored the possibility of rebranding Trump Castle with Hard Rock branding, but having explored fully, frankly the returns as we perceived it just weren't going to meet our criteria," said Rank spokeswoman Susan Donovan. "So we decided not to pursue it any further."

Trump, however, said it retains exclusive, long-term restrictive covenants for theme restaurants, entertainment venues or casinos by Rank's Hard Rock Cafe International or any of its affiliates or subsidiaries in the Atlantic City market.
These "covenants" were included in the pact that established the Hard Rock Cafe and merchandise store in the Trump Taj Mahal in Atlantic City, Trump said.
Trump said it has pursued alternative retheming options for Trump's Castle. The company was not immediately available to comment on those other options.
A decision is expected shortly, and the company said it expects the retheming to be concluded by the 1997 summer casino season.
In June, Rank bought out Hard Rock founder Peter Morton for $410 million, a deal that added 13 Hard Rock Cafes and four franchises to the 15 cafes and 26 franchises Rank already owned.
Trump Hotels' stock fell $1 to $13.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
